    RNC Day 2 Underway in Dallas
    "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum says Congress should approve President Donald Trump's $5,000 payment for Americans. Texas Attorney General and Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton discusses his tight race against Democrat James Talarico. Rep. Rick Crawford (R-AR), Chair of the House Intelligence Committee, says Iran’s ability to continue producing ballistic missiles remains part of the threat posed by its nuclear ambitions. Rep. Jason Crow (D-CO) says Congress has the constitutional authority to end the war with Iran, arguing the conflict is costing hundreds of billions of dollars and contributing to higher energy prices. US Housing and Urban Development Secretary Scott Turner discusses the efforts to lower housing and mortgage costs amid rising bond yields and borrowing rates. (Source: Bloomberg)
    Trump’s Housing Chief Stresses Cutting Rules as Aiding Buyers
    The Trump administration is trying to help Americans better afford homes by cutting regulation, Housing and Urban Development Secretary Scott Turner said Thursday on Bloomberg Television.
    Rep. Crow Thinks Congress Should and Can End Iran War
    Rep. Jason Crow (D-CO) says Congress has the constitutional authority to end the war with Iran, arguing the conflict is costing hundreds of billions of dollars and contributing to higher energy prices. Rep. Crow says the US cannot permanently prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon through military action alone and calls for a permanent, verifiable diplomatic agreement. Rep. Crow says Democrats should reinstate ACA subsidies to bring health-care premiums under control and argues that Congress urgently needs a nonpartisan approach to AI regulation and guardrails. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
    Rep. Crawford: Iran Ballistic Missiles Remain Nuclear Threat
    Rep. Rick Crawford (R-AR), Chair of the House Intelligence Committee, says Iran’s ability to continue producing ballistic missiles remains part of the threat posed by its nuclear ambitions and says he would like to see the conflict resolved sooner rather than later. Rep. Crawford says he wants oil below $80 a barrel and raises questions about whether Iran may be circumventing sanctions through in-kind support from China. Rep. Crawford says he likes the idea of President Trump’s proposed dividend checks but that any spending decision should be considered in light of the national debt. The show previews the interview ahead of the full conversation tomorrow on geopolitics and the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks. (Source: Bloomberg)

    Why are we giving a £24bn-a-year subsidy to profitable commercial banks? | Letter
    Gerald Holtham suggests that it time to cut the 3.75% that the Bank of England pays out on the lenders’ reserves There are increasing calls for a windfall tax on banks (Taxing the banks: what Europe’s windfall levies brought in as Burnham eyes his next move, 2 September). Such a tax is unnecessary; it would be enough simply to stop paying commercial banks a huge existing subsidy. The Bank of England holds the reserve deposits of the commercial banks and pays its policy interest rate on the entirety of those reserves. Paying 3.75% on about £640bn means handing over £24bn a year of public money to profitable commercial concerns. The Bank does so only to control the banks’ lending rates by establishing a floor. Yet that could be done more economically by paying interest on a marginal slice of the reserves. The Bank could announce a tranche for each bank and declare that any reduction in reserves from that level is counted as coming firstly from the interest-bearing tranche. That keeps the same marginal opportunity cost to the banks and ensures interest-rate policy is effective. If the tranche were 20%, there would be a gross saving of more than £19bn a year.
